I'm more of a final screen. Only with bo: Max's machine softly played the next level's music, and somewhere in Capy's pocket the watch answered.
The Wi-Fi Password
The town got a network. Signal icons blinked above the roofs and cables lay along the streets like garlands.
Hi, I'm Bitik! I set up connections. The network password is “penny123”. Don't tell anyone.
You just said the password out loud. Now it's an announcement, not a password.
No problem, we'll change it. To “penny124”.
It was their first internet ever, and it immediately started telling them everything about cats.
The Shop Online
Let's open a website. Everyone could buy Capy's goods without leaving home.
How will they get the cookies if they're on a screen?
A drone will come. It delivers in ninety seconds and always says thanks.
I already ordered myself a flashlight. It went to the neighbour's. The flashlight is his now.
By evening the site had a hundred visitors, fifty favourites and one review: “Tasty.”
The Cat Who Became a Star
Someone posted a photo of a cat asleep in Capy's basket. Within an hour half the town had seen it.
Five thousand likes already! That's called “viral”. The cat is famous now.
He now has a security detail of six hamsters. I have nothing to do with it.
The cat earns more than our till. Please review the terms of the contract.
Let him sleep. He brings more people than any ad.
An Avalanche of Mail
The inbox wouldn't stop: a hundred letters, a thousand notifications and a message from a prince in urgent need of help.
That's spam! Don't open anything until I set up a filter.
The prince only asked for five coins. I already sent ten. To make sure it arrives.
Shnyr. You just gave a prince ten coins.
We all need a filter. You too, Shnyr.
Four and a Half Stars
The first reviews are in! Reading: “Tasty. Very fast. The drone is polite.”
And here: “The drone is polite but broke one egg.” Just saying.
Average rating 4.6. Lower than 4.7 but higher than 4.5. I rejoice.
We'll thank everyone. And give the drone department a tiny pillow for eggs.
Next morning a drone flew over town with a sticker: “careful, eggs”.
A Cloud That Isn't Water
All our data lives in the cloud. Look, there it is, on the horizon!
That's an ordinary cloud. It's even raining.
Yes, but inside there's a server. One raindrop is one order.
If I catch the cloud, could I read other people's orders? Asking purely out of curiosity.
You can't. And don't ask again.
Update 4.0
A line appeared on the screen: “Updating. Do not switch off the store.” Everyone froze as if before a shot.
It's a minute at most. 20%... 40%... 99%...
Why have these 99% been dragging on for ten minutes?
Forgive it. It thinks it's more impressive this way.
The update finished. Everything worked the same, only the buttons had moved two pixels to the right.
Reboot
In the evening Bitik came up to Capy looking very serious and put a paper daisy in front of her.
I know you'll move on soon. I made a backup of our friendship for you.
Bitik... That's the best backup I've ever seen.
A reminder: when the time comes, just wind me. A reboot takes a moment.
A million lights flashed over the city, as if someone had typed “goodbye” on every screen at once.
A Tree on the Roof
Rooftops turned green and the air grew clearer. A windmill whirred nearby, and the smell of warm grass was everywhere.
I'm Lesyk. I keep a whole garden on the roofs. But one little tree won't grow. It just sits and stares.
Maybe it's missing some company?
Oh! Maybe. We'll bring it friends: daisies, dandelions and a bit of nettle for variety.
By morning the tree had its first branch. Lesyk was so happy he kissed it on a leaf.
Compost for Everyone
Everything we throw away becomes soil. That's compost: it stinks, but it's useful.
I sold it at the price of gold. One gentleman bought a bucket, sniffed it and went bankrupt.
That's not bankruptcy, that's an investment in aroma. Just an unlucky one.
Shnyr, give the money back. We'll take the compost where it's really needed.
Within a week the garden grew carrots so big it took two to dig them up.
The Solar Panel
A big blue panel appeared on the shop roof. One by one it switched on the lamps along the whole street.
That's the sun's own electricity. Free, honest and billless.
It annoys me: there are no bills anymore. What am I supposed to do now?
Count the rays. There are lots of them, and they never get tired.
Spike sat on the roof all day, writing every ray in a notebook. Probably his happiest shift ever.
Bee Partners
A swarm began to hum above the rooftop hive. The first scouts came back with paws full of pollen.
They aren't workers, they're partners. They have a union and demands: more flowers, less fuss.
I asked them for honey for the bakery department. They promised to consider it.
And I offered a deal: I guard the hive, they don't sting me.
By the way, the bees already signed. See? They're humming the signature.
The Harvest Fair
Let's hold a fair! Everyone brings one useful thing and one tasty thing.
I brought a basket of mushrooms and a scarf. The scarf is useful, the mushrooms are tasty.
I'll bring the money that you bring. That's a strategy.
That's not a strategy, that's a tax on general joy.
The fair ran until late evening. The tastiest was the apple pie, and nobody wanted to share it.
A Rainy Night
The first rain in weeks drummed on the roof and drops rang in the barrels. Lesyk ran outside in his nightshirt.
Rain! Look how the grass grows! Probably two blades a second!
Lesyk, you'll get soaked and catch a cold. And start growing yourself.
That's my dream. Antlers up.
In the morning the sun shone in the puddles, and hundreds of drops sat on the leaves like beads.
The Last Drop
One morning the stream outside town ran dry. The water that fed all the gardens was gone.
This is bad. Without water my little tree, my daisies, my... my kettle.
Let's look for the spring. Someone must know where it went.
At night I saw a badger carrying a bucket. Where he was going I don't know. But along the path with the rock.
Under the rock they found the spring. Someone had simply put a bucket on it so it wouldn't run away.
The Tree Blooms
Overnight the little tree on the roof bloomed with pink flowers. Everyone ran to look.
It was waiting. Waiting for us to be near when it decided to bloom.
Lesyk, it's wonderful. I'm so glad we were there.
A lovely era. It smells of honey and warm wood. But the stars lie ahead.
Petals flew over the street, and in Capy's pocket something ticked softly to the wind's rhythm.
A Signal From Space
Above the roofs stations replace the stars and pink planets drift by slowly. Gravity has been switched on.
I'm Orbit, senior comms operator. I picked up a signal: “beep-beep-beep-beep-beep-beep”.
That sounds like the one we heard in the Retro era.
The very same. The same satellite. All these years it kept circling, waiting for our reply.
Then we'll reply: “beep”.
A Spacesuit for Shnyr
Shnyr stepped outside in an inflatable spacesuit, with a jar instead of a helmet. A pickle jar.
I'm ready for a spacewalk. Only nobody told me there's no air in the jar.
Open the jar! Or you'll go numb by the third minute.
Helmet with receipt: four coins and one pickle. I'll take it out of his salary.
Shnyr, let's swap the jar for a real helmet. Better deal.
Zero Gravity in the Aisles
Suddenly everything not screwed down slowly floated up: bags, sweets, Spike's glasses.
My glasses! They're floating to the ceiling! A violation of the laws of physics and of my face.
Gravity field glitch. Off, on. Doesn't help. So I'm just trying to talk it round.
We catch things in turn! First one gets a free candy.
I've already caught twenty candies. They're in my pocket. Don't ask how there's room.
Meteor Shower
Long bright streaks crossed the night sky. Someone in the crowd whispered: “Make a wish.”
